categories[0].label: Kleidungsstück
sentences[0].english: I'm looking for trousers in size 38.
sentences[0].why: die Hose — German trousers are SINGULAR: one Hose, where English has a pair.
sentences[1].why: das Hemd — the (men's) shirt; a das-word.
sentences[2].why: das Kleid — the dress; stehen + dative says it suits you.
sentences[3].english: The skirt doesn't fit, it's too tight.
sentences[3].why: der Rock — the skirt is masculine in German; eng = tight.
sentences[4].english: Can I try the jacket on?
sentences[4].why: die Jacke — anprobieren is trying clothes on.
sentences[5].english: In winter I wear a coat.
sentences[5].why: der Mantel — einen shows the der-word in the accusative after tragen.
sentences[6].english: The jumper is made of wool.
sentences[6].why: der Pullover — the jumper; aus names the material.
sentences[7].english: The T-shirt costs only ten euros.
sentences[7].why: das T-Shirt — the borrowed word keeps English spelling and takes das.
sentences[8].english: The shoes are too small, do you have size 42?
sentences[8].why: der Schuh → die Schuhe — the -e plural; sind because they are two.
sentences[9].why: die Socke → die Socken — the -n plural.
sentences[10].english: It's cold – take a woolly hat!
sentences[10].why: die Mütze — the woolly hat; der Hut is the brimmed hat.
sentences[11].english: The blue scarf goes with the jacket.
sentences[11].why: der Schal — the scarf; passen zu says it goes with something.
sentences[12].why: die Bluse — the blouse; weit = too loose, eng's opposite.
sentences[14].english: The belt goes with the trousers.
sentences[14].why: der Gürtel — the belt; ü with the -el ending.
sentences[15].english: The trousers don't fit me – they're too long in the legs.
sentences[15].why: die Hose, singular — and passen + dative (mir) says it doesn't fit me.
sentences[16].english: I don't go out in winter without a woolly hat and a scarf.
sentences[16].why: die Mütze — ohne drops the article in such pairs: ohne Mütze und Schal.
sentences[17].english: My fingers are freezing – where are my gloves?
sentences[17].why: die Handschuhe — plural hand-shoes for cold Finger.
sentences[18].english: The socks don't go with the shoes.
sentences[18].why: die Socken — plural, so passen; zu + dative plural den Schuhen.
help.intro: Buying clothes follows a small, predictable script: finding the department, saying what you are looking for, the size, the colour, trying it on, and the two verbs that decide the sale — passen (fit) and stehen (suit), both with the dative: Die Hose passt mir nicht. Das Kleid steht dir gut. The clothing nouns come with their genders (die Hose, das Hemd, der Rock, der Mantel, das Kleid), and in the shop you will hear them with a colour in front — der blaue Schal, eine rote Jacke. Copy those phrases as chunks for now; the endings on blaue and rote are explained in the adjective quiz a little further on in this module. Shop phrases: Ich suche … Haben Sie das in Größe 40? Kann ich das anprobieren? Wo ist die Umkleidekabine? Ich nehme es.
help.tips[0].title: passen and stehen take the dative
help.tips[0].text: Die Jacke passt mir (fits me) · Das Kleid steht dir gut (suits you) · Die Schuhe passen ihm nicht. Also gefallen: Der Mantel gefällt mir.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The skirt doesn't fit, it's too tight. But the dress really suits you!
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Do you like the jacket? – Yes, and it suits you!
help.tips[0].trap: 'It fits me' becomes 'es passt mir' — dative. 'Es passt mich' is the standard error.
help.tips[0].check.why: passen takes the dative, so 'me' is mir.
help.tips[0].visual.items[2].en: The jacket is too big for me.
help.tips[1].title: The shop script
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Do you have the shirt in blue too, in size M?
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Can I try the trousers on? – Yes, the changing room is at the back there.
help.tips[1].check.q: Haben Sie die Hose auch ____ Größe 38?
help.tips[1].check.why: Sizes and colours both use in: in Größe 38, in Blau.
help.tips[1].visual.moves[0].label: Ask
help.tips[1].visual.moves[1].label: Try on
help.tips[1].visual.moves[2].label: Judge
help.tips[2].title: Sizes, materials, and zu
help.tips[2].text: die Größe (size: 36, 38, 40; S, M, L), aus Wolle / Baumwolle / Leder (made of), zu groß / zu klein / zu teuer (too …). Plural-only: die Hose is singular in German (one pair), but die Schuhe, die Socken are plural.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The trousers are too long, and the wool jumper is too warm.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The shoes are too small. Do you have them in size 42?
help.tips[2].check.q: Die Hose ____ zu lang. (one pair of trousers)
help.tips[2].check.why: die Hose is singular in German, so it takes ist. Things like die Schuhe or die Socken are plural.
help.tips[3].text: tragen = to wear (Ich trage einen Mantel), anziehen = to put on (Ich ziehe die Jacke an), anprobieren = to try on (Kann ich das anprobieren?). Three verbs, three moments.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Put your jacket on, it's cold!
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: Today I'm wearing my new coat.
help.tips[3].check.q: Es ist kalt. ____ deinen Mantel an!
help.tips[3].check.why: Putting a coat on is anziehen. tragen means to wear and has no an.
help.tips[3].visual.marks[0].label: try on
help.tips[3].visual.marks[1].label: put on
help.tips[3].visual.marks[2].label: wear
help.remember[0]: passt mir, steht mir, gefällt mir: clothes talk in the dative.
help.remember[1]: die Hose is one thing; die Schuhe are two.
help.context.en: Hello, can I help you? – Yes, I'm looking for a jacket for winter. – What size are you? – 40. – Here's a nice blue wool jacket. Would you like to try it on? – Yes … it fits me well, but it's too expensive. – The grey coat there is on offer. – Oh, that suits me! I'll take it.
help.mistakes[1].why: anziehen = put on, tragen = wear; don't mix them.
help.mistakes[2].why: A pair of trousers is singular in German.
help.hook: Walk into a German shop, ask for your size, try something on and say 'Das steht mir!' before you pay.
